He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue Boilermakers]]. Ivey has also played for the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|U.S. national under-19 team]] and the [[Detroit Pistons]] who drafted him in 2022. Ivey is the son of [[Niele Ivey]], the coach for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish women's basketball|Notre Dame women's basketball team]]. ==Early life== Ivey grew up playing [[American football|football]], [[basketball]] and [[association football|soccer]], and practicing [[karate]]. He started focusing on basketball as a freshman in high school.{{cite web |last=Hunsinger Benbow |first=Dana |title=The remarkable story of Purdue's Jaden Ivey and his mom, Notre Dame coach Niele Ivey |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/purdue/2021/02/25/purdue-basketball-freshman-jaden-ivey-and-mom-notre-dame-niele-ivey/4510097001/ |website=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |access-date=May 21, 2021 |date=February 25, 2021}} Ivey played for [[Marian High School (Mishawaka, Indiana)|Marian High School]] in [[Mishawaka, Indiana]] in his first three years.{{cite web |last=Noie |first=Tom |title=Former Marian standout Jaden Ivey is a new player, and new person, at LaLumiere |url=https://www.southbendtribune.com/sports/high_school/basketball/former-marian-standout-jaden-ivey-is-a-new-player-and/article_539735d2-37da-11ea-ab6a-ffc2e4a512e5.html |website=[[South Bend Tribune]] |access-date=May 22, 2021 |date=January 16, 2020}} For his senior season, he transferred to [[La Lumiere School]] in [[La Porte, Indiana]], joining one of the top programs in the country.{{cite web |last=Skol |first=Mark Jr. |date=April 29, 2020 |title=Jaden Ivey 'became a man' in senior season at La Lumiere |url=https://www.wndu.com/content/sports/Jaden-Ivey-became-a-man-in-senior-season-at-La-Lumiere-570049351.html |access-date=May 22, 2021 |website=[[WNDU-TV]]}} A consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]] over offers from [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]] and [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]].{{cite web |last=Baird |first=Nathan |title=Purdue basketball receives first 2020 commitment from Mishawaka Marian's Jaden Ivey |url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2019/04/24/mishawaka-marians-jaden-ivey-commits-purdue/3566430002/ |website=[[Journal & Courier]] |access-date=May 22, 2021 |date=April 24, 2019}} ==College career== [[File:Jaden Ivey.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Ivey in January 2021]] Early in his freshman season, Ivey missed five games with a foot injury.{{cite web |last=Carmin |first=Mike |title=Energetic Jaden Ivey returns to Purdue basketball after dealing with foot injury |url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/2020/12/18/energetic-jaden-ivey-returns-purdue-basketball-after-dealing-foot-injury/6543793002/ |website=[[Journal & Courier]] |access-date=May 22, 2021 |date=December 19, 2020}} On January 19, 2021, he made a game-winning three-pointer with five seconds left as part of a 15-point performance in a 67–65 win over [[2020–21 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]].{{cite web |last=Brew |first=Tom |title=Jaden Ivey Gets Emotional After Hitting Game-Winning 3-Pointer for Purdue |url=https://www.si.com/college/purdue/basketball/jaden-ivey-hits-game-winning-three-pointer-purdue-beats-ohio-state |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=May 22, 2021 |date=January 20, 2021}} On March 19, Ivey scored a season-high 26 points in a 78–69 overtime loss to [[2020–21 North Texas Mean Green men's basketball team|North Texas]] at the first round of the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]].{{cite web |last=Pells |first=Eddie |title=North Texas comes up big with 78-69 upset over Purdue |url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-thomas-bell-javion-hamlet-mens-college-basketball-purdue-boilermakers-mens-basketball-147dc487afc23aadfcfe3c6181f36243 |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=May 22, 2021 |date=March 19, 2021}} As a freshman, he averaged 11.1 points and 3.3 rebounds per game, earning [[Big Ten]] All-Freshman Team honors.{{cite web |last=Skol |first=Mark Jr. |date=March 9, 2021 |title=Former local high school basketball star Jaden Ivey named to Big Ten All-Freshman team |url=https://www.wndu.com/2021/03/09/former-local-high-school-basketball-star-jaden-ivey-named-to-big-ten-all-freshman-team/ |access-date=May 22, 2021 |website=[[WNDU-TV]]}}{{cite web |last=Schutte |first=Dustin |title='We've got unfinished business': Jaden Ivey explains decision to return to Purdue |url=https://saturdaytradition.com/purdue-football/weve-got-unfinished-business-jaden-ivey-explains-decision-to-return-to-purdue/ |website=Saturday Tradition |access-date=May 22, 2021 |date=April 27, 2021}} On November 12, 2021, Ivey scored 27 points in a 92–67 win over [[2021–22 Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball team|Indiana State]].{{cite news |title=Ivey, Edey help No. 7 Purdue steamroll Indiana State 92–67 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401372164 |access-date=January 28, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 12, 2021}} On January 30, 2022, he scored 21 points and hit the game-winning three-pointer with 0.6 seconds remaining in an 81–78 win over [[2021–22 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]].{{cite news |title=Ivey 3 in last second, No. 6 Purdue fends off No. 16 Ohio St |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401364412 |access-date=January 30, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 30, 2022}} As a sophomore, he averaged 17.3 points, 4.9 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game. Ivey was named first-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] as well as the All-American Second Team.{{cite press release|url=https://bigten.org/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220308180525/https://bigten.org/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 8, 2022|title=2021-22 Big Ten Men's Basketball Postseason Honors Announced|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=March 8, 2022 |accessdate=March 8, 2022}} On March 31, 2022, Ivey declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{Cite web |last=Carmin |first=Mike |title='This has been a lifelong dream of mine' Purdue's Jaden Ivey declares for NBA Draft |url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2022/03/31/purdue-sbasketball-ophomore-jaden-ivey-nba-draft-nba-lottery-pick/7235032001/ |access-date=March 31, 2022 |website=Journal and Courier |language=en-US}} He was a projected top-five pick in the draft.{{Cite web |title=Jaden Ivey |url=https://nbadraftroom.com/jaden-ivey/ |access-date=March 31, 2022 |website=NBA Draft Room |language=en-US}} ==Professional career== === Detroit Pistons (2022–2026) === Ivey was selected with the fifth overall pick in the [[2022 NBA draft]] by the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|first=Keith|last=Langlois|title=History repeats: Pistons get Ivey, who took Isiah Thomas' path to NBA|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/history-repeats-pistons-get-ivey-who-took-isiah-thomas-path-to-nba|website=NBA.com|date=June 23, 2022|access-date=June 24, 2022}} He made his [[2022 NBA Summer League|summer league debut]] on July 7 against the [[2022–23 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland Trail Blazers]] with 20 points, six rebounds, and six assists in an 81–78 win.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/pistons-news-jaden-ivey-3-word-message-after-dominating-in-summer-league-debut/|title=Pistons rookie Jaden Ivey's 3-word message after dominating in Summer League debut|website=ClutchPoints|last=Salao|first=Renzo|date=July 7, 2022|access-date=July 10, 2022}} On October 19, Ivey made his regular-season debut, putting up 19 points along with three rebounds and four assists in a 113–109 win over the [[2022–23 Orlando Magic season|Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/pistons-news-jaden-ivey-excites-in-detroit-debut-but-another-rookie-resets-a-franchise-record/|title=Jaden Ivey excites in Pistons debut but another rookie resets a franchise record|website=ClutchPoints|last=Villas|first=Rexwell|date=October 19, 2022|access-date=October 19, 2022}} On December 20, Ivey scored 30 points during a 126–111 loss to the [[2022–23 Utah Jazz season|Utah Jazz]].{{Cite web |last=Woods |first=Kory |date=December 20, 2022 |title=Ivey's career-high 30 points not enough as Pistons lose to Jazz, 126-111 |url=https://www.mlive.com/pistons/2022/12/iveys-career-high-30-points-not-enough-as-pistons-lose-to-jazz-126-111.html |access-date=November 13, 2023 |website=mlive.com}} On March 27, 2023, he scored a then career-high 32 points in a 126–117 loss to the [[2022–23 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web |date=March 27, 2023 |title=Middleton leads short-handed Bucks past decimated Pistons |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401469277 |access-date=March 27, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} On November 24, 2023, Ivey scored 25 points during an [[NBA In-Season Tournament|In-Season Tournament]] loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{Cite web |date=November 24, 2023 |title=Haliburton, Turner lead Pacers to 136-113 tournament win over Pistons |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401584135 |access-date=2024-07-02 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}} On February 7, 2024, Ivey scored a career-high 37 points, and added six rebounds and seven assists in a 133–120 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|title=Jaden Ivey scores a career-high 37 points lead Pistons past Kings 133-120|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401585360|website=ESPN.com|date=February 7, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}} On December 26, 2024, in a game against the [[Sacramento Kings]] with the Pistons trailing by three, Ivey connected on a corner three-pointer while being fouled by [[De'Aaron Fox]] and subsequently converted on a four-point play with 3.1 seconds remaining for a 114–113 Detroit victory.{{cite web | last=Zimmerle | first=Will | title=Kings Lose Heartbreaker in Stunning Fashion to Pistons | website=Sacramento Kings On SI | date=2024-12-27 | url=https://www.si.com/nba/kings/onsi/sacramento-kings-news/kings-lose-heartbreaker-in-stunning-fashion-to-pistons-01jg39fbyf72 | access-date=2025-12-07}} On January 1, 2025, Ivey suffered a broken left [[fibula]] after colliding with [[Orlando Magic]] guard [[Cole Anthony]] while attempting to retrieve a loose ball. The next day, it was announced that Ivey would likely miss the remainder of the season after undergoing surgery.{{cite web | last=Maloney | first=Jack | title=Jaden Ivey injury update: Pistons guard could miss remainder of season after breaking fibula, per report | website=CBSSports.com | date=2025-01-01 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/jaden-ivey-injury-update-pistons-guard-could-miss-remainder-of-season-after-breaking-fibula-per-report/amp/ | access-date=2025-01-24}} During the 2025 preseason, Ivey suffered a knee injury against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], sidelining him for the rest of the preseason. He underwent arthroscopic surgery to relieve right knee discomfort and missed at least four weeks of regular-season play.{{Cite web |last=Patterson |first=Hunter |date=October 16, 2025 |title=Pistons guard Jaden Ivey has knee surgery, out at least 4 weeks |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6723965/2025/10/16/pistons-jaden-ivey-knee-surgery/ |access-date=October 16, 2025 |website=[[The Athletic]]}} Ivey made 33 appearances (including two starts) for Detroit in the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging 8.2 points, 2.2 rebounds, and 1.6 assists.{{Cite web|title=Jaden Ivey 2025–26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4433218/jaden-ivey|access-date=February 9, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} === Chicago Bulls (2026) === On February 3, 2026, Ivey was traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] as part of a three team trade that also included the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|title=CHICAGO BULLS ACQUIRE JADEN IVEY AND MIKE CONLEY JR. IN THREE-TEAM TRADE|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/chicago-bulls-acquire-jaden-ivey-and-mike-conley-jr-in-three-team-trade|website=NBA.com|date=February 3, 2026|access-date=February 4, 2026}} He made four appearances for the Bulls, recording averages of 11.5 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 4.0 assists. On March 26, Ivey was ruled out for the remainder of the season due to a left knee injury.{{Cite web|title=Bulls' Jaden Ivey, Jalen Smith out rest of season with injuries|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48313485/bulls-jaden-ivey-jalen-smith-rest-season-injuries|access-date=March 30, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On March 30, 2026, Ivey posted and live streamed on [[Instagram]], where he made critical comments about the [[NBA]]'s involvement in [[Pride Month]] activities, ultimately leading to him being waived by the team on the same day for "conduct detrimental to the team." He also made negative comments about [[Catholicism]], calling it a "false religion".{{Cite web |title=MSN |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/other/jaden-ivey-sparks-concern-with-controversial-messages-on-instagram-catholicism-is-a-false-religion/ar-AA1ZIWYP?ocid=msedgdhp&apiversion=v2&domshim=1&noservercache=1&noservertelemetry=1&batchservertelemetry=1&renderwebcomponents=1&wcseo=1 |access-date=2026-04-06 |website=www.msn.com}} This came in the wake of several social media videos which lasted nearly an hour and an increase in [[evangelism]] in the Bulls locker room which agitated some team staff members.{{cite news |title=Former Piston Jaden Ivey released by Bulls after anti-LGBTQ comments |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2026/03/30/former-piston-jaden-ivey-released-by-bulls-after-anti-lgbtq-comments/89393543007/ |access-date=31 March 2026 |work=The Detroit News |date=30 March 2026}}{{Cite web|title=Bulls waive guard Jaden Ivey after anti-gay comments|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48350464/sources-bulls-waive-jaden-ivey-anti-gay-comments|access-date=March 30, 2026|publisher=[[ESPN]]|language=en}} Ivey responded in a livestream hours after being waived, saying, "They're liars, bro. This is lying. [...] All I'm preaching about is [[Jesus Christ]] and they waived me. They say I'm crazy, right? I'm psycho."{{cite news |last1=Lorenzi |first1=Joel |title=Jaden Ivey on IG Live after being waived by Bulls: 'They're liars, bro. This is lying' |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7159179/2026/03/30/jaden-ivey-waived-bulls-nba-pride-month/ |access-date=31 March 2026 |work=The New York Times |date=31 March 2026}} According to [[Joe Cowley (sportswriter)|Joe Cowley]] of the ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'', Ivey's penchant for evangelizing teammates, coaches and reporters likely led the Bulls to question whether he was capable of "act(ing) like a normal person around his brothers, his 14 other brothers." Cowley believed that Ivey was waived not for merely expressing anti-gay sentiments, but for a larger pattern of behavior that "doesn't go down in an NBA locker room."{{cite web|url= https://youtube.com/watch?v=_3qNxCAE1UY|author1=[[Joe Cowley (sportswriter)|Joe Cowley]]|title=The truth behind the chaotic mess with Jaden Ivey exit|date=March 31, 2026}} ==National team career== Ivey played for the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2021 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in Latvia.{{cite web |last=Fezler |first=D. J. |title=Purdue Basketball's Jaden Ivey to Wear No. 9 for the USA U-19 Team |url=https://www.si.com/college/purdue/basketball/purdue-basketballs-jaden-ivey-to-wear-no-9-for-the-usa-u-19-team |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=July 4, 2021 |date=June 28, 2021}} On July 3, 2021, he scored a team-high 21 points, shooting 7-of-11 from the field, in an 83–54 group-stage win over [[Turkey men's national under-18 and under-19 basketball team|Turkey]].{{cite web |last=Fezler |first=D. J. |title=Jaden Ivey Leads USA U19 FIBA World Cup Team to Victory, Caleb Furst Logs Seven Points |url=https://www.si.com/college/purdue/basketball/jaden-ivey-leads-usa-u19-fiba-world-cup-team-to-victory-caleb-furst-logs-seven-points |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=July 4, 2021 |date=July 3, 2021}} Ivey averaged 12.3 points per game, helping his team win the gold medal, and was named to the all-tournament team.{{cite web |last=Fezler |first=D. J. |title=Purdue's Jaden Ivey, Zach Edey Named to FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup All-Star Team |url=https://www.si.com/college/purdue/basketball/purdue-jaden-ivey-zach-edey-named-to-fiba-u19-basketball-world-cup-all-star-team |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=July 11, 2021 |date=July
